articles.title: AI Visibility Is Not Value
articles.description: A series on AI visibility, source eligibility, platform-specific selection, attribution, measurement, value transfer, platform capture, and the citable archive that remains worth returning to.

articles.title: AI Visibility Is Not Value, Part 1 — AI Visibility Is Not a Direct Optimisation Outcome
articles.description: Appearing in AI-generated answers is not proof that optimisation caused visibility, attribution, traffic, or retained value. AI visibility is an observed output inside a larger source-selection system.

articles.title: AI Visibility Is Not Value, Part 2 — Source Eligibility: Being Available Is Not Being Chosen
articles.description: AI visibility begins with source eligibility, but eligibility is not selection. A source can be crawlable, readable, relevant, and useful without appearing in the final AI answer.

articles.title: AI Visibility Is Not Value, Part 3 — AI Visibility Is Not One Environment
articles.description: AI visibility changes across answer regimes. Some systems retrieve, some synthesise, some cite, some retain users, and some combine those behaviours in different ways.

articles.title: AI Visibility Is Not Value, Part 4 — The Selection Gap
articles.description: The selection gap is the opaque space between source eligibility and final AI answer inclusion. Retrieval, query fan-out, reranking, context construction, and synthesis all separate availability from visibility.

articles.title: AI Visibility Is Not Value, Part 5 — Selected Does Not Mean Cited
articles.description: A source can shape an AI answer without being cited, and a cited source can still be flattened, misrepresented, or denied meaningful credit. Selection, citation, representation, and reward are separate outcomes.

articles.title: AI Visibility Is Not Value, Part 6 — AI Visibility Measurement Cannot Prove Value
articles.description: AI visibility metrics can observe mentions, citations, answer presence, and prompt-level appearances. They cannot by themselves prove causation, representation quality, traffic, conversion, or retained value.

articles.title: AI Visibility Is Not Value, Part 7 — Value Transfer, Retention, and Platform Capture
articles.description: When source material improves an AI answer, who receives the value? AI visibility may produce source value, shared value, or platform capture depending on whether attention, trust, traffic, and relationship value return to the source.

articles.title: AI Visibility Is Not Value, Part 8 — The Citable, Hard-to-Exhaust Archive
articles.description: A source retains value in AI-mediated discovery when it is easy to cite, difficult to exhaust, and worth returning to. The archive becomes a countermeasure to platform capture.

articles.title: AI Visibility Is Not Value, Part 9 — Representation Governance
articles.description: AI visibility becomes a governance problem when platforms mediate who is selected, represented, omitted, attributed, rewarded, and made returnable.

ai-visibility-is-not-value.title: AI Visibility Is Not Value, Part 1 — AI Visibility Is Not a Direct Optimisation Outcome
ai-visibility-is-not-value.description: Appearing in AI-generated answers is not proof that optimisation caused visibility, attribution, traffic, or retained value. AI visibility is an observed output inside a larger source-selection system.

ai-visibility-is-not-value.title: AI Visibility Is Not Value, Part 2 — Source Eligibility: Being Available Is Not Being Chosen
ai-visibility-is-not-value.description: AI visibility begins with source eligibility, but eligibility is not selection. A source can be crawlable, readable, relevant, and useful without appearing in the final AI answer.

ai-visibility-is-not-value.title: AI Visibility Is Not Value, Part 3 — AI Visibility Is Not One Environment
ai-visibility-is-not-value.description: AI visibility changes across answer regimes. Some systems retrieve, some synthesise, some cite, some retain users, and some combine those behaviours in different ways.

ai-visibility-is-not-value.title: AI Visibility Is Not Value, Part 4 — The Selection Gap
ai-visibility-is-not-value.description: The selection gap is the opaque space between source eligibility and final AI answer inclusion. Retrieval, query fan-out, reranking, context construction, and synthesis all separate availability from visibility.

ai-visibility-is-not-value.title: AI Visibility Is Not Value, Part 5 — Selected Does Not Mean Cited
ai-visibility-is-not-value.description: A source can shape an AI answer without being cited, and a cited source can still be flattened, misrepresented, or denied meaningful credit. Selection, citation, representation, and reward are separate outcomes.

ai-visibility-is-not-value.title: AI Visibility Is Not Value, Part 6 — AI Visibility Measurement Cannot Prove Value
ai-visibility-is-not-value.description: AI visibility metrics can observe mentions, citations, answer presence, and prompt-level appearances. They cannot by themselves prove causation, representation quality, traffic, conversion, or retained value.

ai-visibility-is-not-value.title: AI Visibility Is Not Value, Part 7 — Value Transfer, Retention, and Platform Capture

ai-visibility-is-not-value.title: AI Visibility Is Not Value, Part 8 — The Citable, Hard-to-Exhaust Archive

projects.title: AI Visibility Is Not Value
projects.description: A nine-part analysis, with a series overview, separating AI visibility from selection, citation, value transfer and durable audience value.
projects.introduction: Begin with the series argument, then follow the distinction between being available to an AI system, being selected, being cited and retaining any resulting value.

chapters.title: AI Visibility Is Not Value, Part 1 — AI Visibility Is Not a Direct Optimisation Outcome
chapters.description: Appearing in AI-generated answers is not proof that optimisation caused visibility, attribution, traffic, or retained value. AI visibility is an observed output inside a larger source-selection system.

chapters.title: AI Visibility Is Not Value, Part 2 — Source Eligibility: Being Available Is Not Being Chosen
chapters.description: AI visibility begins with source eligibility, but eligibility is not selection. A source can be crawlable, readable, relevant, and useful without appearing in the final AI answer.

chapters.title: AI Visibility Is Not Value, Part 3 — AI Visibility Is Not One Environment
chapters.description: AI visibility changes across answer regimes. Some systems retrieve, some synthesise, some cite, some retain users, and some combine those behaviours in different ways.

chapters.title: AI Visibility Is Not Value, Part 4 — The Selection Gap
chapters.description: The selection gap is the opaque space between source eligibility and final AI answer inclusion. Retrieval, query fan-out, reranking, context construction, and synthesis all separate availability from visibility.

chapters.title: AI Visibility Is Not Value, Part 5 — Selected Does Not Mean Cited
chapters.description: A source can shape an AI answer without being cited, and a cited source can still be flattened, misrepresented, or denied meaningful credit. Selection, citation, representation, and reward are separate outcomes.

chapters.title: AI Visibility Is Not Value, Part 6 — AI Visibility Measurement Cannot Prove Value
chapters.description: AI visibility metrics can observe mentions, citations, answer presence, and prompt-level appearances. They cannot by themselves prove causation, representation quality, traffic, conversion, or retained value.

chapters.title: AI Visibility Is Not Value, Part 7 — Value Transfer, Retention, and Platform Capture
chapters.description: When source material improves an AI answer, who receives the value? AI visibility may produce source value, shared value, or platform capture depending on whether attention, trust, traffic, and relationship value return to the source.

chapters.title: AI Visibility Is Not Value, Part 8 — The Citable, Hard-to-Exhaust Archive
chapters.description: A source retains value in AI-mediated discovery when it is easy to cite, difficult to exhaust, and worth returning to. The archive becomes a countermeasure to platform capture.

chapters.title: AI Visibility Is Not Value, Part 9 — Representation Governance
chapters.description: AI visibility becomes a governance problem when platforms mediate who is selected, represented, omitted, attributed, rewarded, and made returnable.

resources.description: A series on AI visibility, source eligibility, platform-specific selection, attribution, measurement, value transfer, platform capture, and the citable archive that remains worth returning to.
